research_notes: Research for France Travel Scams book. Annecy is a safe destination with lower crime rates than major French cities. Lake Annecy and the Palais de l'Ile are primary tourist areas. Sources include UK FCDO, US Embassy France, France Travel Blog, The World Travel Index.

scams.location: Lake Annecy promenade, Palais de l'Ile, Old Town (Vieille Ville), popular markets
scams.story: Pickpockets operate around Lake Annecy, the Palais de l'Ile, and other popular tourist spots. They often work in pairs or groups, using distraction techniques while an accomplice rifles through bags and pockets. Crowded lakefront promenades during summer are particularly targeted.
red_flags: Groups of people crowding you
Someone creating a distraction
People watching you take out valuables
Bump and grab tactics
how_to_avoid: Use a cross-body bag with zipped compartments
Keep valuables in front pockets or inside jacket pockets
Stay alert in crowded areas
Never leave bags on chairs or the ground in restaurants

scams.location: Plage d'Albigny, Plage des Marquisats, Plage de Talloires, all lakeside beaches
scams.story: Thieves patrol the beaches around Lake Annecy watching for swimmers who leave belongings unattended on the shore. They wait until targets are in the water or facing away, then quickly grab valuables and disappear. Summer months see increased incidents at popular swimming spots.
red_flags: Lone individuals watching beach-goers rather than swimming
People walking slowly near unattended bags
Someone asking you questions while you're away from belongings
how_to_avoid: Never bring valuables to the beach
Leave jewelry and passports at your hotel
Use a waterproof pouch for essentials
Take turns swimming with companions so someone watches belongings

scams.location: Old Town restaurants near Palais de l'Ile, lakefront terraces, areas near major attractions
scams.story: Some restaurants in tourist areas maintain two sets of menus - one for locals with standard prices and another for tourists with inflated prices. Additionally, menus may lack prices entirely, only revealing exorbitant costs when the bill arrives. Hidden charges for bread, water, or cover fees may appear.
red_flags: Menus without prices displayed
Different menus given to different tables
Aggressive steering toward expensive items
Hidden 'service' or 'cover' charges
how_to_avoid: French law requires restaurants to display menus with prices outside
Ask for a menu with prices before ordering
Walk away from restaurants without posted prices
Verify the bill matches menu prices

scams.scam_name: Fake Petition and Charity Clipboard Scam
scams.location: Old Town pedestrian areas, near major attractions, market areas, lakefront promenade
scams.story: Scammers approach tourists with clipboards asking them to sign petitions for supposed charitable causes. After signing, they demand donations of 10-20 euros. The clipboard distracts victims while accomplices pickpocket bags. The petitions feature photocopied logos from legitimate charities but are entirely fraudulent.
red_flags: Clipboard petitioners in English rather than French
Pressure for immediate cash donations
Multiple people working the same area
Someone standing too close behind you
how_to_avoid: Never stop for anyone with a clipboard
Say 'Non merci' firmly and keep walking
Keep hands on your belongings if approached
Legitimate charities do not solicit on streets with petitions

scams.location: Pedestrian areas, lakefront, near tourist attractions
scams.story: A scammer 'finds' a gold ring on the ground near a tourist and asks if they dropped it. When the tourist says no, the scammer offers to sell it as a 'lucky find' for a significant sum, claiming it is valuable gold. The ring is worthless metal. This scam, common in Paris, occasionally appears in smaller French tourist towns.
red_flags: Someone dramatically 'finding' jewelry near you
Ring looks too shiny for something found on ground
Sob story follows the 'discovery'
Request for money as a reward
how_to_avoid: Never engage with anyone claiming to find valuables near you
Say 'Non' and walk away immediately
Do not touch or examine anything offered

scams.location: Pedestrian zones, Old Town, near popular photo spots
scams.story: Scammers aggressively approach tourists and begin tying a 'friendship bracelet' onto their wrist without permission. Once the bracelet is tied, they demand payment, often 10-20 euros or more, becoming aggressive if refused. While attempting to remove the bracelet, accomplices may pickpocket the distracted victim.
red_flags: Someone approaching with string or yarn
Attempts to touch your hand or wrist
Overly friendly strangers offering free gifts
Groups working together
how_to_avoid: Keep your hands in pockets or crossed when walking
Never let strangers touch your hands or wrists
Walk away immediately saying 'Non merci' firmly

scams.location: Trailhead parking areas, scenic viewpoints around the lake, unstaffed parking lots, street parking
scams.story: Thieves target rental cars which are easy to identify by license plates, lack of floor mats, and sterile interiors. They smash windows to steal luggage, electronics, and valuables, sometimes dropping rear seats to access trunks. Parking areas near trailheads and scenic viewpoints are frequently targeted.
red_flags: Parking areas with broken glass on ground
Isolated parking with no surveillance
Anyone watching you load or unload your car
how_to_avoid: Never leave any valuables visible in your car
Remove all items including charging cables
Use staffed parking lots when available
Consider sedan rentals with proper trunks rather than hatchbacks

scams.location: Online - affects pre-trip booking for Annecy accommodations
scams.story: Scammers create fake vacation rental listings for properties in Annecy that either do not exist or belong to someone else. Victims pay deposits or full amounts via bank transfer only to arrive and find no accommodation. Some scammers create sophisticated fake booking websites mimicking legitimate platforms.
red_flags: Prices significantly below market rate
Requests to pay outside official platforms
Poor communication or urgency to book
Empty booking calendars during peak season
how_to_avoid: Only book through official platforms like Airbnb or Booking.com
Never pay via bank transfer or cryptocurrency
Read reviews carefully
Verify property addresses on Google Maps

scams.location: Standalone ATMs, tourist area cash machines, train station ticket machines
scams.story: Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs to capture card data and PINs. Others pose as helpful locals at ATMs or ticket machines, offering assistance while memorizing PIN codes or switching cards. An international ring was busted in 2025 after stealing over 580,000 euros across Western Europe.
red_flags: Loose or unusual attachments on card slots
Strangers offering to help at ATMs
Someone standing too close behind you
Card getting stuck in machine
how_to_avoid: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours
Cover the keypad completely when entering PINs
Decline help from strangers at ATMs
Check card slots for loose attachments before inserting cards

scams.location: Old Town, lakefront, popular photo spots, market areas, near the canal
scams.story: Thieves work in organized groups using distraction techniques. One person creates a diversion - asking for directions, showing a map, dropping items, or staging an argument - while accomplices pickpocket the distracted tourist. They particularly target visitors taking photos or consulting phones and maps.
red_flags: Multiple people approaching simultaneously
Someone creating any kind of scene near you
Person asking for help while others stand nearby
Maps or items thrust in front of you
how_to_avoid: Be immediately suspicious if approached by strangers, especially in groups
Secure your belongings first if someone creates a scene
Keep your phone and wallet in front pockets or secured pouches
Travel with a companion who can watch your back
